discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of time-reversal-invariant topological insulators (the quantum spin Hall effect)
subfield: Condensed matter physics: topological phases of matter
motivation: In 2005 Kane and Mele showed that spin-orbit coupling in graphene-like systems produces a quantum spin Hall state, made of two time-reversed copies of a Chern insulator. They then identified a new Z2 topological invariant that sets this state apart from an ordinary band insulator, even though there is no net Hall conductance. This was a deep conceptual step: topology can be protected by symmetry and does not need a magnetic field. In 2007 Molenkamp and collaborators observed quantized edge conductance in HgTe quantum wells, confirming the prediction, which had been formulated for these materials by Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang. The work generalized to three dimensions and to the classification of topological phases by symmetry. It created the field of topological materials, now studied in thousands of laboratories, with connections to Majorana physics and quantum information. Simple models, unexpected physics, and clean experimental confirmation make this an exemplary Nobel discovery.
